body: All of this code is a lot of magic numbers, and very very easy to accidentally mess up because it's difficult to tell what is what. Could this be turned into a formula to protect against errors in editing it?

1 - I actually think this is easier to read than the previous code. All the values are laid out instead of being hidden behind an algorithm. We should also look at it in parts. First is the geometric part, it is split into groups of 6, corresponding to 2 tris each. If we look at the numbers, it's basically ones and negative ones, and there are patterns, take for instance this group: notice how there is a column of `-0.5` in Y. This tells us that this quad corresponds to the Y- faces, IE the bottom face. The UVs can be easily understood by comparing them with the geometry part, in each column there are always 3 zeroes and 3 ones (or negative ones), they also form a triangular pattern: 2 - The UVs I partly agree, but it has to be done this way. The mesh for CSG has to be manifold, as a result, the faces are generated in different directions. In order to align the side, top and bottom faces they need to be set manually, just like the uv_offset transformations. It is also easier to extend the code when the faces are exposed like that. 3 - This is a 6 sided box, once the code is done, it should not be touched, because there isn't anything to improve. No one should be editing the geometric part at least. 4 - I will see if I can reduce the amount of code that is used and simplify it further.

how about now?

- `compat_mode` now uses a formula.

- removed the branching for scale_uv, now it's only one set of UVs.
as a result, enabling `compat_mode` disables `scale_uv`.

- moved size and offset operations to a for loop.
